purpose: Screen the San Agustin Table 1 labels Siganus guttatus and Siganus spinus against current fish-name authorities and independent Philippine evidence.

method.scope: Focused current-name and Philippine marine/coastal-context review of the verbatim labels Siganus guttatus and Siganus spinus.
method.distinction: The existing strict GBIF crosswalk matches both labels to accepted species-rank names. The current Catalog of Fishes treats both as valid; its abbreviated distribution summaries do not explicitly name the Philippines, but that omission is not evidence of absence. Independent Philippine fisheries literature and a recent field study provide country-level context, not identification of the 2025 San Agustin specimens.
method.evidenceLimit: SEAFDEC's 1986 coastal-fry manual is a historical synthesis, not a current site survey. The 2026 Siargao study collected and examined S. guttatus from named local coastal sites but does not identify the separate San Agustin fish. A Smithsonian Philippine S. spinus voucher is a separate historical specimen, not a Romblon occurrence.
method.sourceReuse: Only concise attributed findings and direct links are retained. No specimen image, sequence, coordinates, or source-table extract was copied. Research-only; no public-app publication or derived checklist is approved.

findings.nameCrosswalk: The existing strict GBIF Backbone crosswalk returned an exact accepted species-rank match (usage key 2390286; confidence 99). The current Catalog of Fishes treats S. guttatus as valid. Preserve the source spelling; the match is not specimen verification.
findings.currentAuthority: The Catalog of Fishes online version updated 13 August 2026 treats Siganus guttatus (Bloch, 1787) as valid. Its abbreviated Indo-West Pacific distribution summary does not explicitly list the Philippines; this omission is not proof of absence and is not counted here as a range discrepancy.
findings.philippineContext: Bagarinao et al.'s SEAFDEC 1986 manual lists S. guttatus among common Philippine siganids and discusses coastal/brackish nursery context. A 2026 field study collected and examined 22 S. guttatus from named coastal stations at Dapa, General Luna, and Pilar on Siargao. These sources support Philippine-context plausibility, not a San Agustin identity or reach.
findings.disposition: Retain the printed species name as a valid-name crosswalk. No new voucher-priority mismatch or authority/range discrepancy is added. The 2025 study specimen and its station remain unresolved.
findings.priority: obtain the RSU catalogue/accession number and any diagnostic or sequence-to-voucher link before projecting this label to a current site-level record

findings.nameCrosswalk: The existing strict GBIF Backbone crosswalk returned an exact accepted species-rank match (usage key 2390216; confidence 99). The current Catalog of Fishes treats S. spinus as valid. Preserve the source spelling; the match is not specimen verification.
findings.currentAuthority: The Catalog of Fishes online version updated 13 August 2026 treats Siganus spinus (Linnaeus, 1758) as valid. Its abbreviated eastern Indian/western Pacific distribution summary does not explicitly list the Philippines; this omission is not proof of absence and is not counted here as a range discrepancy.
findings.philippineContext: Bagarinao et al.'s 1986 SEAFDEC manual lists S. spinus among Philippine siganids and reports siganid catches, predominantly S. spinus and S. canaliculatus, in the Visayas. The Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History separately catalogs USNM 182728 as S. spinus from Malampaya Sound, Palawan, collected during the Albatross Philippine Expedition in 1908. Neither source identifies the 2025 San Agustin material.
findings.disposition: Retain the printed species name as a valid-name crosswalk. No new voucher-priority mismatch or authority/range discrepancy is added. Philippine fishery and museum records are separate context, not a San Agustin site assignment.
findings.priority: obtain the RSU catalogue/accession number and any diagnostic or sequence-to-voucher link before projecting this label to a current site-level record

nextAction: Screen the remaining three Table 1 labels against current fish authorities and locality-resolved Philippine sources. Keep the six voucher-priority mismatch labels and five unresolved authority/range issues in their separate queues. Then seek the RSU voucher/accession crosswalk and resolve the survey's station/locality conflicts before considering occurrence rows.

sources.supports: The 2025 San Agustin survey labels, stated repository holding, missing public specimen accession identifiers, and survey-locality limitations.
